name: swapy-handle

frames.best_why: All six tiles sit in a settled grid with every emoji, title and corner grip visible and no card floating.

tagline: Bright emoji feature cards that rearrange when dragged by a corner grip.
summary: Six flat-colour feature tiles of different widths form a tight grid, each showing an emoji, a short claim and a dotted grip. Dragging a grip lifts the tile, and dropping it on another swaps their places.
appearance: Six saturated tiles in blue, pink, green, yellow, purple and cyan packed into a twelve-column grid, each with a faint dotted grip at its top left. A black emoji and a short bold title sit centred in each card.
behaviour: Pulling a grip frees its tile and marks the slots it passes as drop targets; releasing on a slot swaps the two cards and every tile snaps back to the same fixed height. The reordered map is printed to the console and lasts only until reload.
demo_content: Slogans such as Turbocharge Everything, Brainy Decisions and Save Big, Smile More, each with an emoji.
search_phrases: puzzle tiles you can swap around
use_when: A features block should feel playful and let visitors shuffle the tiles for fun.
avoid_when: Every colour, emoji and width is fixed in the file, and the new order is only logged, never saved.
customise: No props: the six slogans, emoji and colour classes sit in the items array in the file, and the drag config and grid gap are set in the source.
weight_why: Six static colour tiles and a drag handler that only runs during a move.

a11y.note: Dragging is pointer only, and the emoji titles are plain text with no role or keyboard alternative.

issues: Swaps are console-logged only, so the new order is lost on reload.
Each slot takes the item's id instead of its slot id, so the two id sets collide.
The dotted grip is faint grey on pastel and easy to miss.
polish_why: Lively tidy grid with crisp type; the faint grip and clashing palette hold it back.
title: Swapy Handle Bento Grid
